subject.title: Feature Request: tools.cron.tools.deny config option for cron job tool restrictions

question: Should cron jobs get first-class tools.cron.tools.allow/deny, inherit tools.subagents.tools, or keep only per-job toolsAllow plus targeted delivery safeguards?
rationale: The request adds or changes a security-sensitive config surface and scheduled-job tool-access semantics, so code inspection can prove the gap but not choose the product/default policy.

options.title: Add cron-scoped policy
options.body: Introduce tools.cron.tools.allow/deny with explicit precedence against existing policy layers and per-job toolsAllow.

options.title: Inherit subagent policy
options.body: Make cron runs reuse tools.subagents.tools, reducing config surface while coupling two different execution modes.

options.title: Keep per-job only
options.body: Do not add a global cron policy and rely on payload.toolsAllow, docs, and delivery-mode safeguards.

recommendation.title: Add cron-scoped policy
recommendation.body: Introduce tools.cron.tools.allow/deny with explicit precedence against existing policy layers and per-job toolsAllow.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete has recent history on both cron session behavior and scoped conversation capability profiles, and already reviewed this issue's policy gap.
